predecessors.name: Majapahit
predecessors.text: the east of East Java around Jember (Semboro, Lumajang), the same reading the Majapahit dossier uses for the Eastern court

successors.name: Dutch Republic
successors.text: the eastern salient: 'Absorbed into the territory of Dutch East Indies: 1768/1777'

ledger.x: 1478: Blambangan becomes independent as Majapahit dissolves.
1489: the court moves from Semboro to Lamajang (infobox: Semboro 1478-1489, Lamajang 1489-1501).
1519: Blambangan takes over Majapahit's eastern remains after Demak defeats Daha.
1546: the fighting ends with Pasuruan and Pajarakan in Demak's hands.
1546: Blambangan loses Pasuruan and Pajarakan to Demak.
1635: Mataram's war on the Hindu kingdom begins.
1665: Tawang Alun II founds Macan Putih near Banyuwangi.
1768: the Hindu kingdom of Blambangan ends under the Dutch East India Company (infobox 1768/1777).

wars.name: Balinese attack on Blambangan
wars.outcome: No territorial result recorded: 'Blambangan was attacked by Balinese kingdom: 1501'.

wars.name: Demak's conquest of Pasuruan and Pajarakan
wars.outcome: Demak took Pasuruan and Pajarakan from Blambangan.

wars.name: Mataram's conquest of Blambangan
wars.outcome: Blambangan surrendered in 1639 and became a Mataram vassal; it regained independence in 1659.

wars.name: Civil wars in Blambangan
wars.outcome: Infobox 'Civil wars in Blambangan: 1691-1697'; in 1697 'the Balinese Kingdom of Buleleng sent its expedition' and Blambangan 'rejoined Bali' (Mataram page).

certainty.note: No treaty or survey fixes any frontier: the sources give regions (the eastern salient, Pasuruan, Jember, Lumajang), not lines.
